newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta unchanged, dealers suspect intervention.
newsitem.headline: Peseta unchanged, dealers suspect intervention.

text.p: The peseta hardly moved against the mark in midday trade on Friday, but dealers said it remained under pressure and suspected the Bank of Spain was supporting the currency at around 84.90 per mark.

"The peseta continues under pressure and it seems that we will continue with the same story of intervention from the Bank of Spain through third parties," said a dealer who added that he had not seen any intervention directly.
By 1340 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.88/90 per mark, compared to levels seen late on Thursday of 84.77/80.
"This morning, the peseta weakened to 84.95 per mark before firming again rapidly to 84.85 per mark in a rather suspicious move and I think they are still intervening at that level," a dealer said.
Dealers said earlier in the session the Bank of Spain had been buying pesetas versus marks at about 84.85/90.
Nonetheless, they could not quantify the size of the intervention and the Bank of Spain made no comment.
"We will have to wait for February reserve data (which will be announced next week) before we can get an idea about the size of the intervention," a dealer said.
Dealers attributed the downward pressure on the peseta and peripherals to renewed doubts about the viability of the Economic and Monetary Union.
